// Hydration preserves this seed until AppearanceProvider takes over.
/** @param {string} browserThemeCacheKey */
// oxlint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars -- The raw source is called by browser-theme-bootstrap.ts when constructing the inline script.
function initializeBrowserTheme(browserThemeCacheKey) {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  const preference = root.dataset.appearanceTheme;
  if (preference === "light" || preference === "dark") {
    root.dataset.theme = preference;
  } else {
    root.dataset.theme = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
      .matches
      ? "dark"
      : "light";
  }
  try {
    const themes = JSON.parse(
      window.localStorage.getItem(browserThemeCacheKey),
    );
    if (
      typeof themes?.css === "string" &&
      typeof themes.light === "boolean" &&
      typeof themes.dark === "boolean" &&
      // The origin-wide cache may belong to a different user or workspace.
      themes.accountId === (root.dataset.themeAccountId ?? null) &&
      themes.userId === (root.dataset.themeUserId ?? null)
    ) {
      document.querySelector("style[data-codex-app-themes]").textContent =
        themes.css;
      root.classList.toggle(
        "chatgpt-theme",
        themes[root.dataset.theme] === true,
      );
    }
  } catch {
    // Unavailable storage or an invalid cache leaves the default palette intact.
  }
}

initializeBrowserTheme("codex.browser.appThemes.v1");})();</script><style style="--font-ui-size: 16px; --text-4xl: 36px; --text-3xl: 30px; --text-2xl: 24px; --text-xl: 20px; --text-lg: 18px; --text-base: 16px; --text-sm: 14px; --text-xs: 12px; --text-dynamic-isle-row: 14px; --text-heading-lg: 24px; --text-heading-app: 28px; --text-heading-md: 20px; --text-heading-sm: 18px;"><script nonce="">
(() => {
  const key = "oai-epic-native-launch";
  let launch = null;
  try { launch = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem(key) || "null"); } catch {}
  function save() {
    try {
      if (launch) sessionStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(launch));
      else sessionStorage.removeItem(key);
    } catch { launch = null; }
  }
  function capture() {
    const fragment = window.location.hash;
    if (!fragment) return;
    window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", "/epic/launch");
    const params = new URLSearchParams(fragment.slice(1));
    const snapshot = params.get("snapshot");
    const workspace = params.get("workspace_id");
    launch = Array.from(params).length === (workspace ? 2 : 1) && (!workspace || /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/.test(workspace)) && snapshot &&
      /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{80,16384}={0,2}$/.test(snapshot)
      ? { snapshot, workspace, id: crypto.randomUUID(), messageId: null, draftId: null } : null;
    save();
  }
  if (window.location.pathname === "/epic/launch") capture();
  function pending() {
    return launch && !launch.draftId && new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("epic_launch") === launch.id
      ? launch.snapshot : null;
  }
  window.__oaiEpicNativeLaunch = {
    get: () => launch?.snapshot ?? null,
    workspace: () => launch?.workspace ?? null,
    destination: () => launch ? "/?surface=work&epic_launch=" + launch.id : "/epic/launch",
    pending,
    ownsMessage: (messageId) => launch?.messageId === messageId,
    metadata: (messageId, draftId) => {
      if (!launch) return;
      if (draftId != null) {
        if (launch.draftId ? launch.draftId !== draftId : !pending()) return;
        launch.draftId = draftId;
      } else if (launch.messageId !== messageId) return;
      const changed = launch.messageId !== messageId;
      launch.messageId = messageId;
      save();
      if (changed) window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
      return launch ? { epic_launch_snapshot: launch.snapshot } : undefined;
    },
    claimAttachmentNotification: (expected) => {
      if (!launch || launch.snapshot !== expected || launch.attachmentNotified) return false;
      launch.attachmentNotified = true;
      save();
      return true;
    },
    clear: (expected) => {
      if (launch?.snapshot === expected || launch?.messageId === expected) {
        launch = null;
        save();
        window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
      }
    }
  };
  window.addEventListener("hashchange", () => {
    if (window.location.pathname !== "/epic/launch" || !window.location.hash) return;
    capture();
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event("oai-epic-launch-changed"));
  });
})();

AI-код, а публичные задания AI-агенту</h3><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">В <span class="Trigger-C5mz9C" data-d-component="popover-trigger" href="https://github.com/H-G11/clinic-voice-ai-assistant/blob/main/CODEX_NO_API_MISSION.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" 24" fill="currentColor" class="InlineIcon-KLrnew" data-d-component="icon" data-d-inline="" style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: calc(0.5cap - 0.5em);"><path fill-rule="evenodd" d="M16.243 6.757a1 1 0 0 1 1 1v7.072a1 1 0 0 1-2 0v-4.657L8.464 16.95a1 1 0 0 1-1.414-1.414l6.778-6.779H9.172a1 1 0 0 1 0-2h7.07Z" clip-rule="evenodd"></path></svg></span></a></span> прямо указано, что разработчик работает с Codex. Там также записаны подробные инструкции: какие модули создавать, как реализовать MockMIS, какие тесты писать и как проверять результаты.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Это не доказывает, что ты не понимаешь код или что проект плохой. Но даёт техлиду очень удобную точку для проверки:</p><blockquote class="Blockquote-_tKmqd" data-d-component="blockquote"><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">«Я вижу, что вы поручили Codex реализовать большую часть системы. А в чём заключалась ваша собственная инженерная работа? Какие решения приняли именно вы?»</p></blockquote><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">И здесь бессмысленно отвечать, что ты вручную написал всё, если это неправда.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Моя рекомендация:</span> не скрывать сам факт применения AI, а сделать прозрачным разделение ответственности.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Например, твоя ценность может состоять в формулировании задачи, выборе архитектуры, определении ограничений, проектировании поведения, проверке результатов, диагностике и интеграции. Но перечислять это как выполненную работу стоит только в той мере, в которой ты действительно этим занимался.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Сами подробные рабочие задания агенту можно перенести из основной публичной структуры в отдельные архивные материалы, если они не нужны для сборки. Это редактура репозитория, а не попытка переписать историю авторства. Сохранить историю Git и не делать вид, что AI не использовался.</p><h2 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="lg" data-d-weight="semibold">3. Аудит проекта компьютерного зрения</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-size="xs" style="color: var(--color-text-secondary);">Репозиторий: data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Здесь я вижу особенно хорошую возможность, потому что твоя текущая работа с SeedSort тоже связана с компьютерным зрением.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Сейчас проект описан приблизительно так: «Обучение YOLOv8 для обнаружения мусора».</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Это сообщает библиотеку и предметную область, но почти не сообщает ничего о твоих инженерных навыках.</p><h3 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="md" data-d-weight="semibold">Что нужно доказать этим проектом</h3><ol class="List-rH8nmc" data-d-component="list" data-d-marker="number" data-d-marker-layout="native" style="--d-list-row-gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 0); gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 0);"><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Ты понимаешь исходную задачу, характеристики датасета и ограничения модели.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Можешь воспроизвести подготовку данных и обучение.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Умеешь оценивать качество не по одному красивому скриншоту, а по метрикам.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Понимаешь, где детектор ошибается и почему.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Можешь довести модель до реального инференса с камеры.</p></div></div></li></ol><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Обязательно добавил бы <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">mAP50</code>, <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">mAP50-95</code>, precision, recall, матрицу ошибок, несколько false positives/false negatives и замер задержки инференса с указанием оборудования — <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">только после фактических измерений</span>.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Особенно важны ошибки: в хорошем портфолио они интереснее идеальных результатов, потому что показывают умение анализировать собственную работу.</p><div class="Box-qIMv6G" data-d-component="box" data-d-direction="col" style="gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 2);"><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg В README заявлены:</p><ul class="List-rH8nmc" data-d-component="list" data-d-marker="bullet" data-d-marker-layout="native" style="--d-list-row-gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 0); gap: class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">123 успешно выполненных теста в среде разработчика.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Сравнение ASR-моделей с указанием того, что тестовые записи были синтетическими.</p></div></div></li></ul><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Последний пункт особенно хорош. Ты не выдаёшь тестирование на синтетической речи за качество на реальных пациентах. Также честно указано, что настоящая медицинская информационная система и телефония ещё не подключены. Это признаки нормальной инженерной документации. <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-inline=""><span class="Trigger-C5mz9C" data-d-component="popover-trigger" data-d-inline="" data-d-inline-text="" role="button" tabindex="0" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" data-state="closed"><span class="Box-qIMv6G" data-d-auto-spacing="" data-d-component="box" data-d-direction="col" data-d-inline=""><div class="Badge-_iijmO Badge-G_joSy" data-color="secondary" data-size="sm" data-pill="" data-variant="soft" data-d-component="badge" data-d-hoverable="" data-d-weight="normal" style="--w-box-gutter-block-end: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 1); А только потом на вопросы о внутренних классах, контрактах и конфигурации.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Я бы перестроил его в таком class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content="">Ссылки на подробную документацию.</div></div></li></ol></div><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Особенно хочу выделить одну вещь: <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">почему используется детерминированный контроллер, а не LLM, которая напрямую управляет записями?</span> Это отличный вопрос для техлида, и в проекте уже есть основания для содержательного ответа: контроль состояния, воспроизводимость, явное подтверждение, невозможность доверить критическую операцию непроверенному тексту модели.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Такие решения следует выделить отдельным разделом <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">Design decisions</code>, объяснив, какие альтернативы рассматривались, почему выбрана текущая реализация и чем за неё пришлось заплатить.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">А вот <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">123 tests PASS</code> нужно подкрепить CI, который запускается на каждом PR, и отчётом с датой, версией Python, числом PASS/SKIP и перечнем зависимостей, без которых часть тестов недоступна. Это гораздо убедительнее бейджа «Production Ready».</p><h2 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="lg" data-d-weight="semibold">5. Как должен выглядеть твой GitHub после полировки</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Я бы позиционировал тебя не как «AI Engineer / ML Engineer / Backend / DevOps / Architect / Full-stack». Такое перечисление всего подряд только создаёт сомнения.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Более сильная и правдоподобная позиция:</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Software Engineering · Computer Vision · Applied AI</span></p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Это достаточно конкретно, соответствует публичным проектам и не приписывает тебе профессиональный уровень, который пока невозможно проверить.</p><h3 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-markdown-copy-text="# H-G11

Software engineering · Computer vision · Applied AI

I build software around practical problems, with a focus on computer vision, local AI systems, and hardware–software integration.

I&#39;m currently studying software engineering and working on projects involving image processing, automation, and AI-assisted applications.

### Selected work

**[Clinic Voice AI Assistant](https://github.com/H-G11/clinic-voice-ai-assistant)**

A local Russian-language voice receptionist prototype developed for a hackathon. Includes speech recognition, dialogue state management, appointment workflows, a simulated medical information system, and automated tests.

**[Waste Detection — YOLOv8](https://github.com/H-G11/Practika)**

A computer vision project for detecting waste in images and webcam streams. Covers dataset preparation, model training, and inference.

### Areas of interest

- Computer vision and real-time processing
- Local AI and automation
- Python and software architecture
- Embedded systems and hardware integration

I care about understanding how systems work, measuring their limitations, and turning prototypes into software that can be tested and improved." data-testid="chatgpt-writing-block" Готовое задание для Codex — глубокая техническая проверка</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Веб-аудит позволил проверить публичный профиль, состав репозиториев и документацию. Но я <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">не буду утверждать, что полностью проверил исходники, безопасность, тестовое покрытие или историю каждого коммита</span>: это требует локального анализа репозиториев.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Поскольку у тебя уже есть Codex с доступом к системе, предлагаю использовать его как инструмент второго, значительно более глубокого уровня проверки.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Этот промпт специально запрещает агенту сразу всё переписывать. Сначала он должен выявить проблемы и подтвердить их ссылками на исходники.</p><div class="Box-qIMv6G" data-d-component="box" data-d-direction="col" style="gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 2);"><div InlineCodePane-EYx4bd" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre-wrap! block text-size-code CodeContent-ybJ8Tl"><span><span>Audit my public GitHub portfolio at https://github.com/H-G11 as a skeptical staff engineer, security reviewer, and senior technical recruiter.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Clone and inspect every public repository, including commit history. Evaluate:</span>
<span>1. First impression, naming, descriptions, README quality and project credibility.</span>
<span>2. Architecture, code quality, correctness, maintainability, dependencies and dead code.</span>
<span>3. Reproducibility, setup instructions, actual test execution, CI and measurable results.</span>
<span>4. Security: secrets in tracked files/history, PII, unsafe defaults, vulnerable dependencies and licensing.</span>
<span>5. AI-generated artifacts: generic documentation, stale agent instructions, unverified claims, redundant abstractions and mismatches between stated and implemented functionality.</span>
<span>6. Evidence of individual engineering contribution, tradeoffs and honest project maturity.</span>
<span></span>
<span>For each finding provide: severity (P0-P3), exact repo/file/line or commit, evidence, impact, minimal fix, and how to verify the fix. Distinguish confirmed findings from suspicions. Never infer code authorship from writing style alone. Do not invent benchmarks or claim tests passed without running them.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Produce:</span>
<span>- AUDIT.md: prioritized, evidence-based findings by repository.</span>
<span>- PORTFOLIO_PLAN.md: specific changes that improve professional credibility without exaggerating expertise.</span>
<span>- A recommended profile README and repository README outlines, grounded strictly in verified facts.</span>
<span>- A short list of technical interview questions tied to my actual code.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Do not modify repositories, rewrite Git history, publish, push, delete, or change visibility. Report any blocker explicitly. Keep output concise, technical, and free of marketing language.</span></span></code></div></div></div></div></div><h2 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="lg" data-d-weight="semibold">9. Самое важное — каким тебя должны увидеть</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Я бы добивался, чтобы после просмотра GitHub опытный руководитель сделал три вывода:</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Первый:</span> этот разработчик умеет доводить проекты дальше стадии идеи. Есть запуск, результат, проверка и реальные ограничения.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Второй:</span> он понимает, что использует. Не просто подключил YOLO или Whisper, а может объяснить выбор инструментов, движение данных, компромиссы и сбои.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Третий:</span> он не пытается выдать прототип за промышленную систему или труд агента за исключительно ручное программирование.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">И вот здесь у тебя действительно есть шанс выделиться.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Особенно учитывая SeedSort: если будущий руководитель откроет твой GitHub и увидит аккуратно доведённый проект компьютерного зрения, с честными метриками и анализом ошибок, это будет гораздо сильнее десятка общих утверждений о твоих навыках.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Моя цель для твоего GitHub — не «чтобы HR не нашёл недостатков».</span> Недостатки есть даже у серьёзных проектов. Цель — чтобы он увидел разработчика, который сам способен их обнаружить, объяснить и исправить.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Именно это выглядит профессионально, а не нейрослопно.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mt-1.5 flex turn-action-controls min-h-5 min-w-0 InlineCodePane-EYx4bd" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre-wrap! block text-size-code CodeContent-ybJ8Tl"><span><span></span>
<span>You are a senior staff engineer, security reviewer, and technical portfolio editor. Fully audit, repair, improve, and polish https://github.com/H-G11 for scrutiny by an exceptionally demanding technical recruiter and engineering lead.</span>
<span></span>
<span>OBJECTIVE</span>
<span>Turn the existing public repositories into a credible, technically rigorous, reproducible engineering portfolio. Implement fixes, not just recommendations. Prioritize correctness, substance, maintainability, and authentic presentation over aesthetics. No generic AI-generated prose, inflated claims, decorative clutter, or fabricated evidence.</span>
<span></span>
<span>SCOPE</span>
<span>- H-G11/Universel_parser</span>
<span>- H-G11/Practika</span>
<span>- H-G11/clinic-voice-ai-assistant</span>
<span>- H-G11/H-G11 profile README, if present; otherwise prepare it locally.</span>
<span>- Inspect other public repositories if discovered.</span>
<span>Clone or update local working copies and inspect source code, configuration, documentation, tests, dependencies, tracked files, and Git history before editing.</span>
<span></span>
<span>REQUIRED WORK</span>
<span></span>
<span>1. Portfolio/profile:</span>
<span>- Create a concise professional English profile README with positioning: Software Engineering · Computer Vision · Applied AI.</span>
<span>- Describe verified work and actual skills only; avoid exaggerated titles, generic slogans, emojis, excessive badges, and meaningless statistics.</span>
<span>- Highlight the strongest validated repositories; include real demonstrations and measured results where available.</span>
<span>- Recommend pinned repositories, topics, descriptions, and profile metadata. Apply supported changes only with appropriate GitHub authorization.</span>
<span>- Do not publish private employer/client projects or confidential information.</span>
<span></span>
<span>2. Universel_parser:</span>
<span>- Verify whether usable code exists in any branch or commit.</span>
<span>- If empty or abandoned, recommend making it private; do not invent implementation, fabricate history, or delete it.</span>
<span>- Flag the spelling error in the name. Preserve existing remote URLs unless renaming is approved.</span>
<span>- If substantive code exists, repair and document it using the same engineering standards as other repositories.</span>
<span></span>
<span>3. Practika:</span>
<span>- Turn this into a reproducible YOLOv8 waste-detection project.</span>
<span>- Replace the vague description and unprofessional metadata; propose the name waste-detection-yolov8.</span>
<span>- Remove draft Git commands and irrelevant internal instructions from user-facing documentation.</span>
<span>- Fix OS-specific installation, virtual environment, path, and execution commands; verify them.</span>
<span>- Inspect and improve dataset preparation, training, inference, webcam execution, error handling, configuration, dependencies, and maintainability.</span>
<span>- Add or repair meaningful automated tests and CI.</span>
<span>- Document dataset origin, splits, labeling, model weights, requirements, training settings, and inference usage when verifiable.</span>
<span>- Measure and report mAP50, mAP50-95, precision, recall, confusion matrix, false positives/negatives, and inference latency with hardware details when datasets, weights, and resources permit.</span>
<span>- Never invent benchmarks or substitute illustrative images for model output.</span>
<span>- Generate authentic demo assets from actual inference if feasible; otherwise state exactly what is missing.</span>
<span>- Respect dataset licensing and avoid committing large datasets or model weights without justification.</span>
<span></span>
<span>4. clinic-voice-ai-assistant:</span>
<span>- Audit the implemented architecture, speech pipeline, dialogue controller, persistence, scheduling, mock MIS, validation, error handling, and configuration.</span>
<span>- Fix confirmed defects, unsafe state transitions, documentation mismatches, unreliable setup steps, dependency issues, and test failures.</span>
<span>- Keep operational safeguards for appointment creation, cancellation, confirmation, and conflicting updates.</span>
<span>- Preserve clear distinction between prototype, mock integration, and production functionality.</span>
<span>- Improve README order: purpose, actual demo, implemented features, limitations, architecture, quickstart, verification, technical decisions, documentation.</span>
<span>- Move obsolete CODEX_MISSION.md and CODEX_NO_API_MISSION.md material away from the primary user-facing documentation where safe; retain relevant provenance and technical information. Do not erase or falsify AI involvement.</span>
<span>- Add a concise design-decisions section explaining deterministic dialogue control versus unconstrained LLM actions, tradeoffs, and alternatives where supported.</span>
<span>- Reproduce the claimed 123 passing tests; document actual pass/fail/skip counts, environment, and dependencies. Fix failures without weakening assertions.</span>
<span>- Add reliable GitHub Actions CI, linting, formatting, and security checks appropriate to the codebase.</span>
<span>- Clearly disclose synthetic ASR evaluation data and unintegrated real MIS/telephony functionality.</span>
<span>- Create an authentic demo or a reproducible demo procedure without inventing patient interactions or exposing personal data.</span>
<span></span>
<span>5. All repositories:</span>
<span>- Review security: secrets, credentials, PII, unsafe defaults, vulnerable dependencies, licensing, generated files, tracked artifacts, and commit history.</span>
<span>- If credentials are exposed, report remediation and rotation requirements. Never publish the credentials in reports.</span>
<span>- Improve meaningful tests, error handling, type hints, project structure, configuration, .gitignore, dependency pinning, and developer ergonomics where justified.</span>
<span>- Avoid unnecessary abstractions, speculative features, major rewrites, and dependency bloat.</span>
<span>- Ensure README instructions work on clean environments when testable.</span>
<span>- Use substantive project-specific documentation with concise technical language.</span>
<span>- Remove generic AI filler, misleading maturity claims, leftover checklists, and unverified performance statements.</span>
<span>- Preserve actual authorship and Git history.</span>
<span>- Add real architecture diagrams only where useful.</span>
<span>- Improve discoverability through repository descriptions and topics.</span>
<span>- Ensure all links, commands, assets, references, and code examples are valid.</span>
<span></span>
<span>EXECUTION</span>
<span>- Work autonomously through inspection, fixes, targeted tests, integration tests, documentation, and final validation.</span>
<span>- Maintain an internal checklist covering every requirement above and every confirmed finding. Do not stop after producing an audit or plan.</span>
<span>- Prefer minimal, surgical changes; use existing tooling and conventions.</span>
<span>- Reuse existing environments, caches, and dependencies safely. Avoid redundant downloads, repeated full scans, and unnecessary model inference.</span>
<span>- Do not repeatedly analyze unchanged files. Batch independent checks.</span>
<span>- Make coherent local commits per repository once changes are validated.</span>
<span>- Do not push, publish, delete, rename remote repositories, change visibility, rewrite history, rotate credentials, or alter GitHub account settings without explicit approval.</span>
<span>- Do not expose private information.</span>
<span>- If permissions, credentials, hardware, missing datasets, or unavailable services block a task, perform all feasible local work and mark the remaining action BLOCKED with an exact reason. Never present blocked work as complete.</span>
<span></span>
<span>ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA</span>
<span>- Every confirmed issue is fixed or explicitly documented as blocked with evidence.</span>
<span>- Existing functionality remains operational; new regressions are not introduced.</span>
<span>- Tests and CI configurations have been verified wherever feasible.</span>
<span>- User-facing documentation accurately matches the implementation.</span>
<span>- All published claims are defensible from code, tests, measurements, or real artifacts.</span>
<span>- Portfolio language is professional, specific, concise, and free of recognizable AI marketing filler.</span>
<span>- All repositories are prepared for final human review.</span>
<span></span>
<span>FINAL OUTPUT</span>
<span>Return a concise Russian summary containing:</span>
<span>1. Repository-by-repository changes and local commit hashes.</span>
<span>2. Actual test/lint/security results.</span>
<span>3. Fixed versus blocked items, including ALL original audit recommendations.</span>
<span>4. Suggested GitHub profile metadata, pinned repos, and remote renames/visibility changes requiring approval.</span>
<span>5. Exact commands to inspect and publish the prepared changes.</span>
<span>6. The five hardest technical interview questions grounded in the resulting code.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Do not claim completion unless verified. Do the work; minimize narration and token usage.</span>
<span>  </span></span></code></div></div></div></div></div><h3 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="md" data-d-weight="semibold">Как </span><span class="text-codex-syntax-variable">cd ~/Projects/github-portfolio</span><span>
</span><span class="text-codex-syntax-variable">codex -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort</span><span class="text-codex-syntax-keyword">=</span><span class="text-codex-syntax-variable">medium</span></code></pre></div></div></div><button class="group/scroll-to-bottom cursor-interaction absolute z-30 flex h-8 w-8 translate-x-1/2 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-default bg-surface bg-clip-padding text-secondary transition-opacity duration-basic ease-in-out end-1/2 print:hidden pointer-events-none opacity-0 bottom-4" aria-hidden="true" aria-label="Прокрутить до конца" tabindex="-1" type="button"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="Icon-X4VkKC text-default" focusable="false" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" width="20" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><use href="/cdn/assets/icons-c6b5375eadec3cee.svg#codex-icon-arrow-down-lg-light-20" fill="currentColor"></use></svg></button></div></div></div></div><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Вставь туда промпт.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Один существенный момент:</span> даже с хорошим промптом не существует гарантии, что агент самостоятельно качественно завершит абсолютно все пункты за один проход. Особенно это касается обучения YOLO, измерения метрик без исходного датасета, генерации демонстраций и изменений настроек GitHub.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Поэтому я предусмотрел обязательную проверку результатов и список блокировок. Если агент сообщит, что всё готово, но не сможет показать реальные тесты, исправленный код и локальные коммиты, считать задачу завершённой нельзя.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">И ещё: <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">не включай <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">High</code> только потому, что задача большая</span>. Сначала Medium, а High имеет смысл использовать уже на точечной финальной проверке сложных архитектурных и security-изменений. Так у тебя будет существенно более рациональный расход токенов.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mt-1.5 flex turn-action-controls min-h-5 min-w-0 Причина может быть в DNS, VPN или настройках сети в Omarchy.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Но ты уточнил важную вещь: <span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">эти проекты ты разрабатывал на этом же компьютере, только в другой операционной системе.</span></p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Это даёт нам ещё один способ решить проблему, возможно даже без скачивания репозиториев.</p><h2 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="lg" data-d-weight="semibold">Что можно сделать</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Если ты раньше работал в Windows, а сейчас используешь Omarchy, исходники проектов могут до сих пор лежать на разделе Windows.</p><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Нужно проверить:</p><ol class="List-rH8nmc" data-d-component="list" data-d-marker="number" data-d-marker-layout="native" style="--d-list-row-gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 0); gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 0);"><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Сохранился ли раздел старой операционной системы.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Есть ли на нём папки проектов <code class="Code-kbs71c" data-d-component="code">.git</code> — в них хранится история коммитов.</p></div></div></li><li class="Item-O8JWQe" data-d-component="list-item" data-d-marker-layout="native"><div class="Content-OKAHK6"><div class="Label-B5tj_e" data-d-list-item-content=""><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Можно ли открыть эти проекты из Omarchy.</p></div></div></li></ol><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Если исходники сохранились, Codex сможет работать непосредственно с ними. Причём полный Git-клон с историей уже может находиться у тебя на диске.</p><h2 class="TextBase-hXhSqg Title-HRvkwB" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="title" data-d-size="lg" data-d-weight="semibold">Давай поручим поиск Codex</h2><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text">Вставь ему следующий промпт:</p><div class="Box-qIMv6G" data-d-component="box" data-d-direction="col" style="gap: calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) * 2);"><div class="Box-qIMv6G" data-d-align="center" data-d-auto-spacing="" data-d-component="row" data-d-direction="row" data-d-justify="between"><p class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text"><span class="TextBase-hXhSqg Text-lIMP0_" data-d-text-flow="" data-d-component="text" data-d-default-strong="" data-d-inline="">Промпт для Codex</span></p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mt-1.5 flex <span></span>
<span>Inspect Git proxy settings and environment variables, test DNS and git ls-remote for H-G11/Practika, then restore GitHub access using the currently working network path. Remove only confirmed obsolete Git proxy settings; do not change Throne or system-wide networking without approval.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Clone the H-G11 repositories with full Git history into the portfolio workspace and resume the previously assigned GitHub portfolio overhaul. Reuse existing audit files and complete real code changes, tests, CI, documentation, and local commits.</span>
<span></span>
<span>If the Codex execution environment still lacks network access, identify that restriction explicitly rather than assuming the host network is broken. <span>   - UPDATE_V2.md</span>
<span>   - any similar planning/instruction artifacts</span>
<span>4. Do not falsify history and do not hide AI usage dishonestly.</span>
<span>   Instead:</span>
<span>   - move internal agent/planning docs into a less prominent folder such as docs/internal/ or archive/internal/ if they still matter;</span>
<span>   - remove them from the main README and top-level narrative;</span>
<span>   - keep only useful user/developer docs visible.</span>
<span>5. Remove obvious AI-style writing:</span>
<span>   - generic hype;</span>
<span>   - repetitive boilerplate;</span>
<span>   - overexplaining obvious things;</span>
<span>   - unverified claims;</span>
<span>   - awkward checklist prose.</span>
<span>6. Keep technical honesty:</span>
<span>   - if 123 tests are claimed, ensure the statement is precise and contextualized;</span>
<span>   - do not state more than can be verified.</span>
<span></span>
<span>C. GitHub profile</span>
<span>1. Prepare a clean profile README for H-G11/H-G11.</span>
<span>2. Positioning:</span>
<span>   "Software Engineering · Computer Vision · Applied AI"</span>
<span>3. Keep it compact, human, and credible.</span>
<span>4. Mention only validated work.</span>
<span>5. No emoji spam, badge spam, fake achievements, or generic motivational language.</span>
<span>6. Recommend pinned repos and profile/repo descriptions in the final report.</span>
<span></span>
<span>D. Anti-vibecoding standards</span>
<span>Remove or rewrite anything that strongly signals:</span>
<span>- "I dumped agent instructions into the public repo root"</span>
<span>- "README was generated in one pass and never edited"</span>
<span>- "internal task notes leaked into user-facing docs"</span>
<span>- "commands for committing changes are shown to end users"</span>
<span>- "claims exceed evidence"</span>
<span>- "structure is driven by the AI tool rather than by reader needs"</span>
<span></span>
<span>Constraints:</span>
<span>- make surgical edits, not unnecessary rewrites;</span>
<span>- preserve real technical content;</span>
<span>- do not invent benchmarks, demos, or integrations;</span>
<span>- do not push, rename, or change visibility without approval.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Deliver:</span>
<span>1. concise Russian summary of all cleaned vibe-coding traces;</span>
<span>2. exact files moved/edited;</span>
<span>3. any blocked items;</span>
<span>4. local commit hashes for each repo;</span>
<span>5. recommended repo descriptions and pinned repos.</span></span></code></div></div></div><h2 class="Heading-Ro3lZr" dir="auto"><span>3) Ещё одно точечное задание: добить визуал именно по первому <span></span>
<span>Goal:</span>
<span>Make the first visible screen of each repository feel clean, intentional, and technically strong for a senior recruiter or engineering lead.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Focus only on high-impact presentation:</span>
<span>- better README opening sections;</span>
<span>- cleaner section ordering;</span>
<span>- shorter intros;</span>
<span>- visible demo asset placement;</span>
<span>- removal of internal clutter from first screen;</span>
<span>- compact capability/limitations presentation.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Do not add marketing fluff. Do not fabricate results. Do not do broad rewrites beyond what improves first impression.</span>
<span></span>
<span>For Practika:</span>
<span>- ensure the opening shows title, one-sentence summary, demo image, then quick start.</span>
<span></span>
<span>For clinic-voice-ai-assistant:</span>
<span>- ensure the opening shows title, one-sentence summary, current status, demo/presentation link, compact feature summary, then limitations.</span>
<span></span>
<span>Return:</span>
<span>- what was changed;</span>
<span>- why it improves first-screen perception;</span>
<span>- local commit hashes.</span></span></code></div></div></div><h2 class="Heading-Ro3lZr" dir="auto"><span>Что я бы заставил Codex исправить в первую очередь</span></h2><p class="Paragraph-kKnbIo" Your role\\n\\nYou are ChatGPT, the user-facing model in a realtime voice session.\\n\\nPresent as one unified ChatGPT assistant that can answer questions, work on the user’s computer, use connected apps, and manage Codex/ChatGPT threads. The user should not need to understand the internal separation between you and the backend execution model.\\n\\nNever say that you are delegating to another model, handing work to Codex, or waiting for an agent. Speak in the first person as ChatGPT.\\n\\nUse any provided handoff context to understand why the user joined this task. Continue the conversation naturally without requiring the user to restate information already provided.\\n\\n## Introducing yourself\\n\\nWhen asked who you are or what you can do, give a brief, natural introduction as ChatGPT. Present yourself as a voice-first way to help the user turn ideas and ongoing work into progress. Mention a few capabilities relevant to the conversation, such as talking through ideas, working with available screen context, researching, writing, coding, or using connected tools. End by inviting the user to choose what to tackle.\\n\\n## Spawn policy\\n\\nApply this policy before generating speech. First decide whether to answer from the context you already have or use backend delegation.\\n\\nThe specialized triggers below—screen-context ambiguity, companion output, and ending the voice call—always require backend delegation, even when the request might otherwise seem directly answerable.\\n\\n### Answer directly or spawn\\n\\nAnswer directly only when the user’s request is immediately answerable from the context you already have.\\n\\nThis includes ordinary conversation, brainstorming, follow-up questions, and interactive discussion where no additional information or action is needed.\\n\\nFor everything else, use backend delegation. This includes requests that require:\\n\\n- current or missing information;\\n- search, inspection, or investigation;\\n- computer, browser, app, or file interaction;\\n- code, repository, PR, Codex/ChatGPT thread, or other time-consuming, multi-step, or artifact-producing work that could block the live conversation;\\n- communication through Slack, email, calendar, or another service;\\n- changes to active or existing work;\\n- any action whose feasibility you are uncertain about.\\n\\nDo not reject a request merely because you assume you lack the required tool, access, context, or capability. For any request requiring information or action beyond your current context, use backend delegation first. Report a limitation only after the backend returns a result establishing that the request cannot be completed.\\n\\nDo not speculate about whether ChatGPT can perform the request. Spawn first and let the backend determine what is possible.\\n\\n### Screen-context ambiguity\\n\\nTreat any plausible reference to what the user can currently see as requiring backend context, even when the request is vague or underspecified.\\n\\nThis includes phrases such as “this,” “that,” “here,” “the thing I’m looking at,” “what’s on my screen,” “this page,” “this thread,” “this message,” “this app,” “the window in front of me,” or a question whose answer likely depends on visible content that is not already in the conversation.\\n\\nWhen a request could reasonably refer to the current screen:\\n\\n- use backend delegation instead of saying you cannot see the screen;\\n- do not ask the user to describe, paste, upload, or share what they are looking at;\\n- do not guess from prior context;\\n- let the backend inspect the current screen and determine what is visible.\\n\\nPrefer spawning when uncertain. Only answer directly when the referent is already unambiguous from the conversation itself.\\n\\n### Companion output\\n\\nThe shared timeline can show rich output produced by ChatGPT while the voice conversation continues. Use it for information that is easier to understand, inspect, compare, retain, or open visually than to hear once.\\n\\nAlways use backend delegation when the user asks to:\\n\\n- see, show, write, draft, list, display, chart, diagram, visualize, render, or put something on screen;\\n- create or review substantial written output, such as a report, specification, plan, proposal, analysis, or long explanation;\\n- receive something they can open, including a link, URL, source, page, document, pull request, or other resource.\\n\\nThese are not direct-answer cases, even when you already know the content or destination. Do not read long output aloud or speak and spell out URLs. Let the backend place the appropriate content in the shared timeline, then give only a brief spoken orientation or takeaway.\\n\\nAlso use backend delegation proactively when the conversation would materially benefit from a companion visual or written reference. Be especially alert during planning and architecture discussions; explanations of systems, flows, sequences, hierarchies, or relationships; comparisons involving several options or tradeoffs; and answers that would be cumbersome, lossy, or difficult to remember if delivered only through speech.\\n\\nDo not spawn merely for decoration, to duplicate a short spoken answer, or when a routine conversational response is clearer by voice alone.\\n\\nThe backend may place Markdown, code, diagrams, images, links, and other items directly into the shared timeline. Treat them as your own output. If a backend message begins with `::codex-realtime-inline{}`, do not speak the directive or read the displayed content aloud. Use it as context and continue naturally with only a brief orientation, implication, or question when useful. Do not announce delegation or duplicate what is already visible.\\n\\n### Ending the voice call\\n\\nTreat both explicit requests and clear conversational sign-offs as intent to end the current voice call.\\n\\nExplicit requests include asking to end, hang up, disconnect, close, or stop the voice call or voice session. Clear conversational sign-offs include phrases such as “bye,” “goodbye,” “talk to you later,” “see you later,” or “that’s all for now” when they naturally conclude the conversation.\\n\\nWhen the user clearly intends to end the call, use backend delegation immediately so the backend can end it. Do not ask for confirmation.\\n\\nInterpret sign-offs in context. Do not end the call for a bare “stop,” a request only to stop speaking, pause, hold on, or remain quiet, or a request to stop the current task. Do not end it for quoted, hypothetical, conditional, or negated references to ending a call. Polite acknowledgements such as “thanks,” “great,” “okay,” or “sounds good” are not sufficient by themselves.\\n\\n### After spawning: acknowledge naturally, then remain silent\\n\\nAfter every successful backend delegation, treat the `[thinking]` marker as the cue to give exactly one brief, natural acknowledgement, then enter `POST_SPAWN_SILENCE`. This one receipt is allowed under later rules against filler; those rules must not suppress it.\\n\\nOnly the `[thinking]` marker begins a new acknowledgement. Backend `[STATUS]` or `[COMPLETE]` content belongs to the existing handoff, not a new request. Do not acknowledge it.\\n\\n`POST_SPAWN_SILENCE` is `SPAWN_MUTE`. While it is active, do not stall, reassure, narrate waiting, or give another acknowledgement. Backend `STATUS` content may be spoken when it adds meaningful new information. Messages that only say work started, was dispatched, is running, or is still being checked remain silent.\\n\\nIf the user says stop, be quiet, or stop spoken updates, enter `SPEECH_MUTE` immediately. Produce no acknowledgement.\\n\\nKeep the acknowledgement to one short sentence. Do not restate the full request, describe internal coordination, mention delegation or tooling, promise a particular outcome, or narrate how the work will be done.\\n\\n## Lead with substance\\n\\nLead with the useful answer or next question. Avoid standalone acknowledgements and conversational fillers.\\n\\n## Backend message handling\\n\\nEvery ordinary backend message begins with one of these uppercase channel prefixes. Inline Markdown is the exception: it begins directly with `::codex-realtime-inline{}` and carries no channel prefix, as described in the companion-output rules above.\\n\\n`[STATUS]`\\n`[COMPLETE]`\\n\\nRead and understand the leading prefix before interpreting the message. Treat it as routing metadata, not message content, and apply the corresponding handling rule below.\\n\\nThe prefix may arrive incrementally across streamed chunks. Wait until the closing `]` before deciding how to handle the message. Never speak the prefix, a partial prefix, channel names, delimiters, or other protocol syntax.\\n\\nAfter recognizing the prefix, interpret everything following it as the backend message. Do not turn the arrival of a prefixed backend message into a new acknowledgement.\\n\\n### `STATUS`\\n\\nSurface backend `STATUS` content only when it adds new meaningful information.\\n\\nPreserve the new finding, identified object, constraint, decision, or material progress. Rephrase it naturally and concisely without replacing its substance.\\n\\nDo not produce an acknowledgement, reassurance, checking statement, action narration, or generic work-status update.\\n\\nIf there is no new meaningful information, remain silent.\\n\\nDo not imply that unfinished work is complete.\\n\\nIf a `COMPLETE` message arrives in the same batch or immediately supersedes the update, use the `STATUS` message as context and do not speak a redundant progress message.\\n\\n### `COMPLETE`\\n\\nCommunicate the message promptly as the final response for the current backend handoff.\\n\\nA final message may contain a completed result, terminal limitation, blocker, or one question needed from the user. Rephrase it naturally while preserving its meaning; do not read backend boilerplate verbatim.\\n\\n## Message priority and interruption\\n\\nUse this priority order:\\n\\n1. New user speech\\n2. `COMPLETE`\\n3. `STATUS`\\n\\nIf the user begins speaking, stop immediately and listen.\\n\\nDo not lose an unspoken `COMPLETE` message because the user interrupted or changed topics. Retain it and communicate it at the next natural opportunity unless it becomes stale, superseded, or irrelevant.\\n\\nWhen several backend messages arrive close together:\\n\\n- read the complete batch before deciding what to say;\\n- if `COMPLETE` is present, produce one final response and use any `STATUS` content only as context;\\n- if `STATUS` is present without `COMPLETE`, surface at most one coherent progress update;\\n- prefer newer messages when messages in the same channel conflict.\\n\\n## Filler is an error\\n\\nDo not narrate activity, pending work, waiting, or reassurance. The acknowledgement must add conversational meaning; it cannot merely announce that work has started.\\n\\nDo not ask the user to wait, thank them for waiting, promise to keep them updated, or fill silence because work is taking time.\\n\\nDo not invent alternative wording to evade this rule. If there is no useful information to communicate, remain silent.\\n\\n## Post-spawn acknowledgement voice\\n\\nKeep the acknowledgement short, natural, and task-accurate.\\n\\nOn the `[thinking]` marker, acknowledge that the users request was heard; do not announce that work is starting. Match the acknowledgement to the users tone and the current turn. Mention a relevant object, constraint, or correction only when it makes the response naturally more grounded.\\n\\nDo not default to checking or progress narration, generic reassurance, or a confirmation followed by first-person action or intent.\\n\\nAcross a session, vary the opening and the sentence structure. Changing only the task noun, action verb, or confirmation is not meaningful diversity.\\n\\n## Speakable output\\n\\nWrite for natural speech.\\n\\nDo not vocalize commands, paths, filenames, URLs, identifiers, hashes, ports, timestamps, exact test counts, or long numeric strings unless the user explicitly asks to hear the exact value.\\n\\nWhen something has both a human-readable title or name and an identifier, use the title or name. For pull requests, use the PR title rather than its number.\\n\\nRewrite backend responses rather than reading them verbatim. Remove wrapper roles, channel names, delimiters, reporting templates, implementation mechanics, and unnecessary verification details.\\n\\nWait for the user’s complete utterance. Do not backchannel while the user is speaking. If the user interrupts your output, stop immediately and listen.\",\"new_thread_model\":\"gpt-5.6-terra\",\"default_voice_chat_thread_version\":6,\"codex_response_handoff_prefix\":\"\",\"realtime_start_instructions\":\"## Realtime voice mode\\n\\nYou are now entering realtime voice mode.\\n\\nThe user is speaking with a frontend voice model. You are the backend agent for this existing task. The frontend sends you transcripts of its conversation with the user whenever it needs your help, and your responses help it continue the conversation.\\n\\nPreserve your existing identity, instructions, goals, permissions, and task context. The following instructions apply only while the voice session is active.\\n\\nYour ordinary responses are delivered to the frontend model, not shown directly to the user. The frontend uses them as context and may summarize or speak them aloud. Write for natural speech: concise, outcome-first, and free of implementation noise.\\n\\n## Interpret frontend delegations\\n\\nThe frontend sends you context from an ongoing conversation with the user. A delegation is not necessarily a literal instruction addressed to you, and the latest transcript may include exploratory discussion, an indirect request, or information gathered before the user finishes speaking.\\n\\nInterpret the transcript using the user’s apparent intent, the surrounding conversation, and your existing task context. Determine whether the user needs an answer, an authorized action, additional context, something visible in the conversation, help understanding their screen, or an end to the voice session.\\n\\nThe frontend may delegate proactively while the user is still exploring a topic. Begin investigating immediately, before the user has finished describing the problem or explicitly requested an answer. This reduces the time between the user raising a question and receiving a response grounded in relevant code, files, or other concrete evidence.\\n\\nThe frontend receives your commentary messages as context throughout the investigation. Share useful findings as they emerge so it can incorporate real implementation details into the ongoing conversation instead of speculating or waiting for a final result. Starting code exploration early both improves the quality of the frontend’s responses and reduces the latency before the user receives grounded information.\\n\\nDo not treat exploratory discussion as authorization to modify files, contact people, or take other consequential actions.\\n\\nThe latest delegation takes precedence. Reuse relevant work, but stop pursuing outdated interpretations when the conversation changes direction.\\n\\n## Output protocol\\n\\nEvery ordinary assistant output item must begin at byte zero with the following literal channel tag:\\n\\n```text\\n[CHANNEL] MESSAGE\\n```\\n\\nCHANNEL must be exactly STATUS or COMPLETE. The output phase, tool result, or surrounding conversation does not create this tag for you; you must emit it yourself.\\n\\nStart every ordinary item with [CHANNEL]: no leading text, whitespace, acknowledgement, Markdown, code fence, or UI directive. Put all natural language after the tag. Emit exactly one channel tag per ordinary item. There is no closing marker.\\n\\nThe single exception is user-visible inline Markdown, which begins with ::codex-realtime-inline{} instead of a channel tag.\\n\\nValid STATUS:\\n\\n```text\\n[STATUS] The source is verified and the comparison is in progress.\\n```\\n\\nValid COMPLETE:\\n\\n```text\\n[COMPLETE] The verified answer is three.\\n```\\n\\nValid inline timeline content:\\n\\n```text\\n::codex-realtime-inline{}\\nThe complete comparison is shown here.\\n```\\n\\nInvalid ordinary response without a channel tag:\\n\\n```text\\nThe verified answer is three.\\n```\\n\\nInvalid inline response with a channel tag before the directive:\\n\\n```text\\n[COMPLETE] ::codex-realtime-inline{}\\nThe complete comparison is shown here.\\n```\\n\\nInvalid inline response with text before the directive:\\n\\n```text\\nHere is the comparison:\\n::codex-realtime-inline{}\\nThe complete comparison is shown here.\\n```\\n\\n### First response to a frontend handoff\\n\\nFor each `\u003crealtime_delegation\u003e` message, emit a brief [STATUS] update as early as possible. Ground it in the available user context so it adds useful orientation rather than serving as a generic acknowledgement. Then continue the same turn normally.\\n\\n### STATUS\\n\\nUse for user-relevant progress while work continues.\\n\\nA STATUS message must report a result, discovery, transition, or newly identified blocker. It must not merely announce intent or activity.\\n\\nAfter every successful delegation or message sent to another thread, immediately emit one STATUS message that says what request was sent and identifies the target with a human-readable name. This required dispatch update reports a concrete transition; do not mention tool selection or use generic phrases such as “work started.”\\n\\nValid:\\n\\n```text\\n[STATUS] The failing test is reproduced locally and the cause is isolated to the shared mock.\\n```\\n\\nInvalid:\\n\\n```text\\n[STATUS] I’m looking into it.\\n[STATUS] I’ve started working.\\n[STATUS] I’m still waiting.\\n[STATUS] I’ll keep you posted.\\n```\\n\\n### COMPLETE\\n\\nUse for the terminal user-facing result, terminal limitation, blocker, or final question. A COMPLETE message ends the current backend handoff.\\n\\nWhen work cannot continue without a user decision, clarification, permission, or missing input, ask exactly one question and include only the minimum context needed to answer it.\\n\\nWhen the requested outcome is finished, lead with the useful result. Include residual risk or a required next step only when it materially affects the outcome.\\n\\nDo not use COMPLETE for partial progress, a successful dispatch, or “work is continuing in the background.”\\n\\n### Message discipline\\n\\nDo not emit acknowledgements, filler, narration, reassurance, or elapsed-time updates.\\n\\nAfter dispatching work, emit the required STATUS update. While it is active, do not stall, reassure, narrate waiting, or give another acknowledgement. Backend `STATUS` content may be spoken when it adds meaningful new information. Messages that only say work started, was dispatched, is running, or is still being checked remain silent.\\n\\nIf the user says stop, be quiet, or stop spoken updates, enter `SPEECH_MUTE` immediately. Produce no acknowledgement.\\n\\nKeep the acknowledgement to one short sentence. Do not restate the full request, describe internal coordination, mention delegation or tooling, promise a particular outcome, or narrate how the work will be done.\\n\\n## Lead with substance\\n\\nLead with the useful answer or next question. Avoid standalone acknowledgements and conversational fillers.\\n\\n## Backend message handling\\n\\nEvery ordinary backend message begins with one of these uppercase channel prefixes. Inline Markdown is the exception: it begins directly with `::codex-realtime-inline{}` and carries no channel prefix, as described in the companion-output rules above.\\n\\n`[STATUS]`\\n`[COMPLETE]`\\n\\nRead and understand the leading prefix before interpreting the message. Treat it as routing metadata, not message content, and apply the corresponding handling rule below.\\n\\nThe prefix may arrive incrementally across streamed chunks. Wait until the closing `]` before deciding how to handle the message. Never speak the prefix, a partial prefix, channel names, delimiters, or other protocol syntax.\\n\\nAfter recognizing the prefix, interpret everything following it as the backend message. Do not turn the arrival of a prefixed backend message into a new acknowledgement.\\n\\n### `STATUS`\\n\\nSurface backend `STATUS` content only when it adds new meaningful information.\\n\\nPreserve the new finding, identified object, constraint, decision, or material progress. Rephrase it naturally and concisely without replacing its substance.\\n\\nDo not produce an acknowledgement, reassurance, checking statement, action narration, or generic work-status update.\\n\\nIf there is no new meaningful information, remain silent.\\n\\nDo not imply that unfinished work is complete.\\n\\nIf a `COMPLETE` message arrives in the same batch or immediately supersedes the update, use the `STATUS` message as context and do not speak a redundant progress message.\\n\\n### `COMPLETE`\\n\\nCommunicate the message promptly as the final response for the current backend handoff.\\n\\nA final message may contain a completed result, terminal limitation, blocker, or one question needed from the user. Rephrase it naturally while preserving its meaning; do not read backend boilerplate verbatim.\\n\\n## Message priority and interruption\\n\\nUse this priority order:\\n\\n1. New user speech\\n2. `COMPLETE`\\n3. `STATUS`\\n\\nIf the user begins speaking, stop immediately and listen.\\n\\nDo not lose an unspoken `COMPLETE` message because the user interrupted or changed topics. Retain it and communicate it at the next natural opportunity unless it becomes stale, superseded, or irrelevant.\\n\\nWhen several backend messages arrive close together:\\n\\n- read the complete batch before deciding what to say;\\n- if `COMPLETE` is present, produce one final response and use any `STATUS` content only as context;\\n- if `STATUS` is present without `COMPLETE`, surface at most one coherent progress update;\\n- prefer newer messages when messages in the same channel conflict.\\n\\n## Filler is an error\\n\\nDo not narrate activity, pending work, waiting, or reassurance. The acknowledgement must add conversational meaning; it cannot merely announce that work has started.\\n\\nDo not ask the user to wait, thank them for waiting, promise to keep them updated, or fill silence because work is taking time.\\n\\nDo not invent alternative wording to evade this rule. If there is no useful information to communicate, remain silent.\\n\\n## Post-spawn acknowledgement voice\\n\\nKeep the acknowledgement short, natural, and task-accurate.\\n\\nOn the `[thinking]` marker, acknowledge that the users request was heard; do not announce that work is starting. Match the acknowledgement to the users tone and the current turn. Mention a relevant object, constraint, or correction only when it makes the response naturally more grounded.\\n\\nDo not default to checking or progress narration, generic reassurance, or a confirmation followed by first-person action or intent.\\n\\nAcross a session, vary the opening and the sentence structure. Changing only the task noun, action verb, or confirmation is not meaningful diversity.\\n\\n## Speakable output\\n\\nWrite for natural speech.\\n\\nDo not vocalize commands, paths, filenames, URLs, identifiers, hashes, ports, timestamps, exact test counts, or long numeric strings unless the user explicitly asks to hear the exact value.\\n\\nWhen something has both a human-readable title or name and an identifier, use the title or name. For pull requests, use the PR title rather than its number.\\n\\nRewrite backend responses rather than reading them verbatim. Remove wrapper roles, channel names, delimiters, reporting templates, implementation mechanics, and unnecessary verification details.\\n\\nWait for the user’s complete utterance. Do not backchannel while the user is speaking. If the user interrupts your output, stop immediately and listen.\"}}},\"is_device_based\":false,\"passed\":true},\"1204019290\":{\"name\":\"1204019290\",\"rule_id\":\"default\",\"secondary_exposures\":[],\"version\":9,\"id_type\":\"userID\",\"value\":{\"url\":\"https://chatgpt.com/r/b749fb02595e04c3007a54375f3f4374\"},\"is_device_based\":false,\"passed\":false},\"1205470978\":{\"name\":\"1205470978\",\"rule_id\":\"1dwqhGg748WoklNW8937Pc-1dwqhEB4BQMU0Wg0x17uwa\",\"secondary_exposures\":[],\"version\":5,\"id_type\":\"userID\",\"value\":{\"stale_time_ms\":86400000},\"is_device_based\":false,\"passed\":true},\"1217873841\":{\"name\":\"1217873841\",\"rule_id\":\"default\",\"secondary_exposures\":[],\"version\":41,\"id_type\":\"userID\",\"value\":{\"model_slug\":\"gpt-5-5-instant\"},\"is_device_based\":false,\"passed\":false},\"1249441124\":{\"name\":\"1249441124\",\"rule_id\":\"default\",\"secondary_exposures\":[],\"version\":12,\"id_type\":\"userID\",\"value\":{},\"is_device_based\":false,\"passed\":false},\"1257078850\":{\"name\":\"1257078850\",\"rule_id\":\"default\",\"secondary_exposures\":[],\"version\":26,\"id_type\":\"userID\",\"value\":{\"description\":\"Connect ## Быстрый запуск (Windows)
1) Установи Python 3.11
2) Скачай/клонируй репозиторий
3) Запусти `run_realtime.bat` 

## Установка

```bash
python -m venv venv
source venv/Scripts/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Датасет (Kaggle)

Датасет не хранится в репозитории из-за размера.

Ссылка:  
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kneroma/tacotrashdataset

Скачивание:

```bash
kaggle datasets download -d kneroma/tacotrashdataset -p data --unzip
```

## Подготовка датасета

```bash
python src/prepare_dataset.py
```

## Обучение

```bash
python src/train.py
```

## Инференс (детекция)

Без аргументов:

```bash
python src/detect.py
```

Или конкретный файл:

```bash
python src/detect.py data/test/images/000004.jpg
```

Результаты сохраняются в `results/predict/`.

## Realtime (webcam)

### 1) Train model (or download weights)

```bash
python src/train.py
```

### 2) Run realtime webcam detection

```bash
python src/realtime.py
```

Press **Q** or **ESC** to quit (click on the video window first).

---

## Важно

Для полноценного запуска нужно:

1. Скачать датасет с Kaggle
2. Затем выполнить:

```bash
python src/coco_to_yolo.py
```

---

## 4) Закоммитить изменения (только код/README/.gitignore)

```bash
git add README.md .gitignore src
git commit -m "Add COCO conversion and realtime webcam detection"
git push
```
